shots.name: Shooter Lane / Plunger
shots.notes: Manual plunger on the far right; sends the ball around the top of the playfield. Hold the left flipper during the plunge for a Super Skill Shot.

shots.name: Top Lanes (Tall Grass)
shots.notes: Rollover lanes across the back; the flashing lane is the standard skill-shot target and builds Bonus X (caps 20x). Feeds the bumpers below.

shots.name: Tall Grass Pop Bumpers
shots.notes: Two lit pop bumpers representing tall grass; fill the Discover gauge to spawn wild Pokemon. Fed by the right orbit around the back and weak left-orbit shots.

shots.name: Left Orbit (Bulbasaur)
shots.notes: Outer left orbit; a clean shot loops the back and returns to the right flipper. Home shot for Bulbasaur story mode; feeds Bulbasaur TEAM loops.

shots.name: Psyduck Target / Sneak-In
shots.notes: Low left, gating the left-orbit entrance. Pro = standup target; premium-le = Sneak-In scoop/subway with ball-saver. Secret skill-shot target (3x value).

shots.name: Left Ramp (Squirtle)
shots.notes: Steepest shot; one-way gate registers partial shots and allows backhands. The CATCH! capture shot and Squirtle home shot. premium-le adds the Whirlpool spinning bowl.

shots.name: Left Berry Target
shots.notes: Standup flanking the left side of the Squirtle ramp entrance; part of the 2x Playfield / Berry set.

shots.name: Right Berry Target
shots.notes: Standup flanking the right side of the Squirtle ramp entrance; part of the 2x Playfield / Berry set.

shots.name: Center Berry Target
shots.notes: Third berry target left of the Pokedex captive ball. Hit when flashing to arm 2x Playfield; hitting it during 2x extends the timer +5s.

shots.name: Poke Ball Lock Mech
shots.notes: Illuminated Poke Ball at the left-ramp area used to catch Pokemon. Pro = static RGB with ball-stop post; premium-le = animatronic ball-lock (LE = Master Ball sculpt).

shots.name: Training Targets
shots.notes: Left-side targets that train/heal Pokemon, extend mode timers, and are required for Travel. One heal per swap in Rival Battles.

shots.name: BATTLE Targets - Left Bank
shots.notes: Left 3-bank of the center Battlefield that spells B-A-T-T-L-E; qualifies Team Rocket Multiball and deals Rival Battle damage. Also the 'Battlefield' combo shot.

shots.name: BATTLE Targets - Right Bank
shots.notes: Right 3-bank of the center Battlefield spelling B-A-T-T-L-E; deals Rival Battle damage.

shots.name: Center Lane
shots.notes: Straight-up center shot between the BATTLE banks; Team Rocket MB start / super-jackpot lane, faint-jackpot lane, and arena-bonus cash-out.

shots.name: Meowth Balloon
shots.notes: Team Rocket bash toy that lowers over the arena when BATTLE is spelled; bash 3x (+2 each subsequent MB) to light multiball at the lane beneath it.

shots.name: Pokedex Captive Ball
shots.notes: Triple captive ball; the game's hub shot. Scans Pokemon, finishes story modes, cashes out combos (Poke Balls = combo length), scores super jackpots. Best hit from the left flipper.

shots.name: Right Ramp (Pikachu)
shots.notes: Encircles the Pikachu toy and feeds the right flipper fast. Home shot for Pikachu vs. Raichu multiball, Pikachu Hurry-Up (TEAM), and the Charizard mini-wizard start.

shots.name: Right Orbit (Charmander)
shots.notes: Right orbit; fastest route into the Tall Grass bumpers. Home shot for Charmander story mode and Charmander Super Spinner.

shots.name: Charmander Spinner
shots.notes: Optical spinner at the front/entrance of the right (Charmander) orbit; ~30k-100k per spin depending on mode/TEAM boost.

shots.name: Town Scoop (Chansey)
shots.notes: Far-right scoop; starts Rival Battles, collects Mystery awards, Travel, and Extra Balls. Ejects fast/dangerously - catch it live on the left flipper.

shots.name: Town Targets (Chansey)
shots.notes: Two standups near the town, reachable mainly via slingshot bounces; complete to light the outlane ball save.

shots.name: Action Button (Lockbar)
shots.notes: Lockbar button. Press while it blinks green to bank Team Rocket / Pikachu add-a-ball; also locks Pikachu Hurry-Up value, scores whirlpool prizes, and fires Pokedex Assist.

steps.detail: Part of the 3-berry arm sequence

goals.summary: Complete a story mode (or first Team Rocket super jackpot) to qualify a 2x shot multiplier, hang it on your money shots, and cycle a full set to unlock 3x.
goals.reward: 2x -> 3x scoring on your best shots for the rest of the ball

steps.detail: Best target - captures and Team Rocket jackpots both score here; affects everything that shot scores

steps.action: Hang the next multiplier on the right-orbit spinner
steps.detail: Second-priority multiplier shot

goals.reward: Super jackpot up to 100M (200M with 2x playfield)

steps.action: Complete all four story modes
steps.detail: Bulbasaur, Squirtle, Pikachu and Charmander - playing all four lights the ramp, and every one you finish raises the scoring inside

steps.action: Start the mini-wizard at the lit right ramp
steps.detail: Starts only when nothing else is running; four-ball multiball

steps.action: Hit 2 lit shots per phase, then the captive ball
steps.detail: Scores combined value x balls in play; each phase base = 10% of that story mode's total score

steps.action: After all 4 phases, hit the center lane super jackpot
steps.detail: Cap 100M (200M with 2x playfield); Last Chance adds a ball if down to one

steps.detail: Chain catches (Forest 1, Lake 3, Desert 6...) and battles toward the Lucario challenge

goals.reward: Super jackpot worth the accumulated jackpot value, plus a shot multiplier

goals.summary: Farm Poke Balls by cashing combos at the Pokedex until the total lights an extra ball, then collect it at the town scoop.

steps.action: Start combos on the ramps and orbits
steps.detail: Every shot in a live combo chain is worth one Poke Ball

steps.action: Extend the chain with the left orbit
steps.detail: Longer chains cash out for more balls, so keep the combo alive before finishing

steps.action: Cash the chain at the Pokedex captive ball
steps.detail: Awards Poke Balls equal to the full combo length; repeat until the extra ball lights

steps.action: Collect the lit extra ball at the town scoop
steps.detail: The scoop kicks out fast - be ready to catch it on the left flipper

goals.title: Steer the Outlane Ball Save
goals.summary: Pokemon's outlane ball save only ever guards one outlane at a time, and which side that is can be changed. Completing the town targets lights it, and a flipper press moves the protection across, so the save can be waiting on whichever outlane the ball is actually drifting toward.
instructions: Complete the town targets to light the outlane ball save
Check which outlane is currently lit, because only one side is protected at a time
Press either flipper button to alternate the save to the other outlane
Move it to the side the ball is heading for before the ball gets there
Each time the save is used, one more completion of the town targets is needed to light it again
goals.reward: Outlane ball save protection on the side you choose

goals.title: Catching Gets Harder Every Time
goals.summary: Catches are the currency the whole game runs on. They are what lights rival battles, what opens the next habitat, and what pads your bonus at the end of the ball. The first one is nearly free and every one after it stretches the sequence, so a catch made early in a ball is worth far more than the same catch made late.
instructions: Rattle the bumpers and roll the top lanes — working those switches is what turns up a wild Pokemon.
Once one has been found, shoot the Pokedex captive ball to scan it. That starts the catch hurry-up and switches on a short ball save.
Hit the lit purple shots to build the catch value, then finish at the left ramp to actually make the catch.
The first catch of a game needs only one purple shot. Every catch after it needs more.
Catching lights the scoop on the right for a rival battle. The first battle costs one catch, and each battle after it costs more than the one before.
Every Pokemon you catch also builds your end-of-ball bonus, so a long ball with several catches pays you twice.
goals.reward: Rival battles unlocked at the scoop, progress toward a new habitat, and a bigger end-of-ball bonus

goals.title: Swap Your Pokemon for a Type Advantage
goals.summary: Rival battles are the one place where type matchups change the math. You always open with Pikachu, but the scoop lets you bench it and bring in another member of your party, and choosing the type that beats what you are facing turns a slow grind into a quick knockout.
instructions: Every rival battle opens with Pikachu, an electric type.
Ramp, orbit and Battlefield shots deal damage in your active Pokemon's type: fire for Charmander, water for Squirtle, electric for Pikachu, grass and poison for Bulbasaur.
During the battle the scoop flashes in the colour of a Pokemon on your bench. Shoot it to bring that one in.
Tap the right flipper to change which party member the scoop is offering before you take the shot.
An attack that is strong against what you are facing does more damage. Charmander's fire punishes the forest's bug types, and Bulbasaur's grass punishes the lake's water types.
Complete the training targets during a battle to heal whichever Pokemon is out at the time.
If your active Pokemon is knocked out, the next one in your party takes over.
goals.reward: Faster knockouts and a party still standing when the next battle starts

goals.title: Travelling Between Habitats
goals.summary: The game is built as a journey across four habitats, and every one of them has to be earned. You begin in the forest and only move on once you have caught something there and taken on that habitat's rival team — and because each habitat further along the journey demands more catches before its battle will even light, most games never leave the trees.
instructions: Every game begins in the forest, where bug types dominate.
Catch a Pokemon in the habitat you are currently in.
Take on that habitat's rival battle.
Complete the training targets by the left orbit as well, outside of a story mode — catch, battle and training together are what open travel to a new habitat.
The lake is stocked with water types; the desert and the mountain are the other two habitats.
Each habitat further along needs more catches before its rival battle will light, which is why most games end in the forest.
goals.reward: A new habitat with different Pokemon to find and a differently typed rival team

drills.title: Held-Flipper Center Lane
drills.text: Hold the left flipper through a full-strength plunge so the ball diverts onto the playfield, then put it in the center lane. Landing it completes BATTLE outright and lowers the balloon, so the plunge is worth as much as several playfield shots.

drills.title: Own the Left Ramp
drills.text: Alternate a backhand off a left-flipper cradle with a live shot off the right flipper. It is the steepest shot on the game and the one every capture locks in at, so a ramp you can only hit one way is a ramp you will miss under pressure.

drills.title: Pokedex From a Cradle
drills.text: Trap on the left flipper and hit the captive ball from there rather than swinging at it on the fly. Everything routes through this shot — scans, story-mode finishes, combo cash-outs — so make it a shot you take deliberately.

drills.title: Town Scoop Kickout
drills.text: Shoot the town scoop and have the left flipper ready before the eject fires — it comes out fast and hard. Catch it live rather than swinging at it, then reset and go again.

drills.title: Right, Left, Hub
drills.text: Right ramp, backhand the left ramp off the return, finish at the captive ball. The one-way gate on the left ramp registers a partial shot, so a backhand that only half makes it still keeps the chain alive.

drills.title: Berry Arm Sequence
drills.text: Hit each flanking berry twice, then take the center berry while it flashes. The two flanking targets sit right at the left-ramp entrance, so work out which flipper reaches each one cleanly before you need the doubler.

actionButton.label: Action Button
actionButton.how: Read the color and you know what the button holds. Green means an add-a-ball is waiting, red means a Pokedex Assist is loaded. In between it locks in hurry-up values and grabs whirlpool prizes while the game is holding your ball for you.

uses.when: BATTLE re-spelled during Team Rocket Multiball
uses.what: Press while it blinks green to bank an add-a-ball — the standard way to stretch that multiball out.

uses.when: Pikachu Hurry-Up, ball held at the right ramp
uses.what: Mash to drive the value up from 6M; only the number showing at release actually scores.

uses.when: Ball spinning in the Squirtle whirlpool
uses.what: Press to take the prize showing right then at double value; every spin swaps the award.

uses.when: CATCH! hurry-up running, button blinking red
uses.what: Spends a Pokedex Assist to collect the lit shot for you — it can't take the final catch shot.
Press and the game scores your most valuable lit shot without you shooting it.

howItPlays.objective: Pokemon (Stern, 2026) sends you across four habitats to catch Pokemon and win Rival Battles. Discover and catch wild Pokemon, run the four story modes, and climb toward the Charizard and Lucario wizard goals.
loop: Plunge a lit top lane to build your bonus multiplier, then feed the ball down into the Tall Grass bumpers, which turn up a wild Pokemon.
Scan it at the Pokedex captive ball to start the CATCH hurry-up, hit the purple shots, and finish at the left ramp to make the catch.
Spell BATTLE on the center banks to lower the Meowth balloon, bash it, and shoot the lane beneath it for Team Rocket Multiball.
Start a story mode at its home shot -- left orbit, left ramp, right orbit or right ramp -- to earn a shot multiplier you hang on your best shot.
Take a caught Pokemon into a Rival Battle at the town scoop and chain battles so the faint jackpot keeps compounding.

lights.name: Top Lanes (Tall Grass)
lights.lit: The flashing rollover is your skill-shot lane, and every top lane you complete steps up the Bonus multiplier, which climbs toward a twenty-times ceiling.
lights.then: Roll the lit lane, then let the ball settle down into the Tall Grass bumpers below -- working the bumpers fills the Discover gauge and turns up a wild Pokemon for you to scan.

lights.name: Pokedex Captive Ball
lights.lit: The triple captive ball is the game's hub -- it scans a discovered Pokemon to start the catch, cashes combos into Poke Balls, finishes story modes, and collects super jackpots.
lights.then: Trap on the left flipper and take it from the cradle rather than swinging on the fly. Scanning starts the CATCH hurry-up with a short ball save; the first catch of the game needs a single purple shot and each one after asks for more.

lights.name: BATTLE Banks & Meowth Balloon
lights.lit: The two center Battlefield banks spell B-A-T-T-L-E, and the center lane spots any letter you miss; completing the word lowers the Meowth balloon over the arena.
lights.flashing: With BATTLE spelled, the Meowth balloon flashes -- bash it three times to light the lane directly beneath it.
lights.then: Shoot the lit lane under the balloon to start Team Rocket Multiball. Re-spelling BATTLE during the multiball feeds add-a-balls off the action button rather than jackpots, which is how you keep it alive.

lights.name: Berries (2x Playfield)
lights.lit: The two flanking berries take two hits each, and then the center berry flashes to arm 2x Playfield.
lights.flashing: The flashing center berry starts twenty seconds of doubled scoring; hitting it again during that window adds a few seconds toward the cap.
lights.then: Layer 2x Playfield over your biggest window -- a multiball or a super-jackpot burst -- so everything scores double while it runs.

lights.name: Story Home Shots
lights.lit: Each story Pokemon lives at its own shot -- Bulbasaur at the left orbit, Squirtle at the left ramp, Charmander at the right orbit, Pikachu at the right ramp -- and three hits to a home shot begins that mode.
lights.then: Finishing a story mode qualifies a shot multiplier you hang on your money shot; playing all four lights the right ramp for the Pikachu vs. Charizard mini-wizard.

lights.name: Town Scoop (Rival Battles)
lights.lit: The far-right Chansey scoop starts a Rival Battle once you have caught a Pokemon, and also hands out Mystery awards, Travel to a new habitat, and lit extra balls.

control.effect: during a battle the scoop flashes in a benched Pokemon's colour, and a tap of the right flipper changes which party member it is offering, so you can bring in whichever type has the advantage over what you face
control.when: before you shoot the flashing scoop mid-battle

lights.then: Keep your party alive and chain battles: the faint jackpot at the center lane is multiplied by every Pokemon you have beaten, so it compounds into the biggest sustained points source on the game. Catch, battle, and clear the training targets to open Travel to the next habitat.

howItPlays.laneChangeNote: Clear the two town targets and the outlane ball save lights up, then tap either flipper to slide that protection to whichever outlane the ball is drifting toward. Only one side is guarded at a time, and each save you spend burns it -- clear the town targets again to relight it.

scoring.text: Plunge safely to a lit top lane and let the bumpers spawn your first Pokemon, then start Pikachu's easy two-ball multiball at the right ramp. Clear the town targets early so the outlane ball save is lit and can be steered before you take any risks.
Put your first shot multiplier onto the left ramp, arm 2x Playfield at the berries, and queue Team Rocket Multiball by spelling BATTLE so you can stack it over a story mode.

Run all four story modes and the right ramp lights for the Pikachu vs. Charizard mini-wizard, a four-ball multiball with a super jackpot up to a hundred million -- doubled under 2x Playfield. Chaining Rival Battles for the compounding faint jackpot is the biggest sustained engine underneath it.
